name: Corpse Collector
epithet: The one the quiet things will answer
description: A pathway of endings. Its powers ask what was done to a thing after the thing has stopped being able to lie about it — which makes a murder into a witness, and makes its walker into somebody the living find difficult to be near. Cheap in spirituality, expensive in sanity, and the only pathway here that gets easier the worse the case is.

sequences.title: Corpse Collector
sequences.description: You collect what is left over. Bodies, mostly, and the things they were holding. In return, the leftovers have begun to answer questions — not in words, but in a flat certainty that arrives before you have finished asking.
sequences.narrative: You drank it in the back of a mortuary van on the Tussock run, because the Church's index said the role would want somewhere honest to start. The next body you lifted told you where it had been carried from, and you had to put it down again.

requirements.label: Close a case for the Nighthawks
Obtain the Coffin Bearer formula (requisitioned, or a copy)
Digest the Corpse Collector potion — do the work, and do it properly

advancement.ritualText: Blackthorn's cellar room has been swept and the candles are the cheap tallow kind, at your insistence: the rite wants a pauper's funeral, not a gentleman's. You mark the circle. Then you drink, and something takes the weight of you as though you were being carried.

temptation.label: Drink it now, and let the ground settle afterwards
temptation.description: You have not finished being what you are. Taking the next role early is a burial with the earth thrown in first.

sequences.title: Coffin Bearer
sequences.description: What you take up, you may set down where you like — and a door is only a thing standing between you and somewhere you have been asked to carry something. The living have begun crossing the street when they see you coming, and they could not tell you why.
sequences.narrative: You carried your first box alone, at the wrong end and against the weight, and it was not heavy. Afterwards you sat on the churchyard wall for an hour working out what that meant.

requirements.label: Digest the Coffin Bearer potion — carry somebody, in company
Be seen bearing a stranger to the ground

advancement.ritualText: You do this one at four in the morning, which is when the trade does its honest work. Smith attends and says nothing, and afterwards admits he has never watched this pathway climb before.

temptation.label: Drink it now, and let the ground keep what it takes
temptation.description: The role you are wearing is not finished with you. Putting another on top of it is how bearers stop coming back up the path.

sequences.title: Gravekeeper
sequences.description: You keep a ground now, whether or not anybody deeded it to you, and the ground keeps you. Ask a question standing on it and the answer arrives with the weight of a verdict. People obey that voice and resent you for it afterwards.
sequences.narrative: Somewhere between the rite and the morning you acquired the habit of counting the people in a room and quietly noting which of them will be first. You have not managed to stop.

requirements.label: Digest the Gravekeeper potion — hold a ground, and mean it

advancement.ritualText: The circle is marked in grave-earth this time, because at this rung the method stops pretending to be a metaphor. Old Neil reads it out twice and asks you, twice, to say your own name.

temptation.label: Drink it now, and be buried in the office
temptation.description: An Undertaker taken early does not walk out of the rite so much as attend it.

sequences.title: Undertaker
sequences.description: The trade that is welcome in every house and wanted in none. Locks conclude their business when you approach them, the recently dead give you a full account, and you can put on the profession like a coat and walk through any door in the city.
sequences.narrative: You went back to Narcissus Street in the coat, and the same constable who moved you on in the spring held the door and called you sir, and did not recognise you at all.
